MC	<p>1d04_0d95</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #825200;">Gene F</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #825200;"><i>fuzzy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #825200;">Gene F</span> colonies are covered in soft, fine filaments, giving them a fuzzy, cotton-like texture.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006d61;">Gene W</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #006d61;"><i>webbed</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006d61;">Gene W</span> colonies produce delicate, web-like strands that connect neighboring colonies in a cobweb pattern.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: ++, fw, ++, fw"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #5c6419;">Gene A</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #5c6419;"><i>amber</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #5c6419;">Gene A</span> cells develop a rich yellow-orange pigmentation, giving the colony a warm, amber hue.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #973756;">Gene M</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #973756;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. MC	<p>7080_fb66</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #91460e;">Gene C</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #91460e;"><i>clumpy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #91460e;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #2f6290;">Gene H</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #2f6290;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. MC	<p>bdb0_918d</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #825200;">Gene F</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #825200;"><i>fuzzy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #825200;">Gene F</span> colonies are covered in soft, fine filaments, giving them a fuzzy, cotton-like texture.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #3957b2;">Gene R</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #3957b2;"><i>rusty</i></span>' phenotype. MC	<p>9773_6ac6</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #a23025;">Gene D</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #a23025;"><i>doubled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #a23025;">Gene D</span> cells display double or multiple budding, with several buds emerging simultaneously.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #356d1d;">Gene M</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #356d1d;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #356d1d;">Gene M</span> colonies are small, dense, and secrete compounds that inhibit the growth of nearby colonies.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: ++, dm, ++, dm"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>43ac_309f</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #006d61;">Gene R</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #006d61;"><i>rusty</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006d61;">Gene R</span> colonies develop a reddish-brown pigmentation, reminiscent of rusted metal.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #8f367c;">Gene W</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #8f367c;"><i>webbed</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #8f367c;">Gene W</span> colonies produce delicate, web-like strands that connect neighboring colonies in a cobweb pattern.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: ++, rw, ++, rw"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>b4fe_073e</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #825200;">Gene K</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #825200;"><i>knotted</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #825200;">Gene K</span> cells grow in twisted, coiled shapes, resulting in a knotted or gnarled appearance.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #3957b2;">Gene M</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #3957b2;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #3957b2;">Gene M</span> colonies are small, dense, and secrete compounds that inhibit the growth of nearby colonies.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: ++, km, ++, km"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>bbe9_538f</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #91460e;">Gene F</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #91460e;"><i>fuzzy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #91460e;">Gene F</span> colonies are covered in soft, fine filaments, giving them a fuzzy, cotton-like texture.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006d61;">Gene W</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #006d61;"><i>webbed</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006d61;">Gene W</span> colonies produce delicate, web-like strands that connect neighboring colonies in a cobweb pattern.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: ++, fw, ++, fw"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>1cab_237f</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #91460e;">Gene F</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #91460e;"><i>fuzzy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #91460e;">Gene F</span> colonies are covered in soft, fine filaments, giving them a fuzzy, cotton-like texture.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006d61;">Gene P</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #006d61;"><i>pebble</i></span>' phenotype. MC	<p>3ff5_7da7</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #006886;">Gene C</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #006886;"><i>clumpy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006886;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #973756;">Gene H</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #973756;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #973756;">Gene H</span> cells develop long, thread-like filaments that extend outward, creating a hairy, shaggy texture on the colony.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: ++, ch, ++, ch"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 5px 8px;">8,000</td></tr></table><h6>Step-by-Step Instructions</h6><ul> <li>Step 1: Find the row for the Parental Type for all three genes.</li> <li>Step 2: Looking at only your two genes, assign PD, NPD, TT.</li> <li>Step 3: Determine if the two genes are linked.</li> <ul><li>PD &gt;&gt; NPD &rarr; linked; PD &approx; NPD &rarr; unlinked</li></ul> <li>Step 4: Determine the map distance between the two genes.</li> <ul><li>D = &half; (TT + 6 NPD) / total = (3 NPD + &half; TT) / total</li></ul></ul><h5>Determine the distance between the two genes MC	<p>dac4_154a</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #356d1d;">Gene E</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #356d1d;"><i>elephant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #356d1d;">Gene E</span> cells absorb excessive amounts of liquid, resulting in giant, swollen cells.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #6041c3;">Gene F</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #6041c3;"><i>fuzzy</i></span>' phenotype. MC	<p>9e9e_8719</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #1d6e49;">Gene C</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #1d6e49;"><i>clumpy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #1d6e49;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #7c3e9c;">Gene W</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #7c3e9c;"><i>webbed</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #7c3e9c;">Gene W</span> colonies produce delicate, web-like strands that connect neighboring colonies in a cobweb pattern.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: ++, cw, ++, cw"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 5px 8px;">8,200</td></tr></table><h6>Step-by-Step Instructions</h6><ul> <li>Step 1: Find the row for the Parental Type for all three genes.</li> <li>Step 2: Looking at only your two genes, assign PD, NPD, TT.</li> <li>Step 3: Determine if the two genes are linked.</li> <ul><li>PD &gt;&gt; NPD &rarr; linked; PD &approx; NPD &rarr; unlinked</li></ul> MC	<p>6324_84fa</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #356d1d;">Gene M</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #356d1d;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #356d1d;">Gene M</span> colonies are small, dense, and secrete compounds that inhibit the growth of nearby colonies.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #8f367c;">Gene W</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #8f367c;"><i>webbed</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #8f367c;">Gene W</span> colonies produce delicate, web-like strands that connect neighboring colonies in a cobweb pattern.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: ++, mw, ++, mw"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>faf2_25a1</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #5c6419;">Gene H</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #5c6419;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #5c6419;">Gene H</span> cells develop long, thread-like filaments that extend outward, creating a hairy, shaggy texture on the colony.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #8f367c;">Gene W</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #8f367c;"><i>webbed</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #8f367c;">Gene W</span> colonies produce delicate, web-like strands that connect neighboring colonies in a cobweb pattern.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: ++, hw, ++, hw"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>268e_9d45</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #1d6e49;">Gene C</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #1d6e49;"><i>clumpy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #1d6e49;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #8f367c;">Gene T</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #8f367c;"><i>toxic</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #8f367c;">Gene T</span> secretes a toxic compound that inhibits or kills other microbial colonies nearby.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: ++, ct, ++, ct"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 5px 8px;">5,800</td></tr></table><h6>Step-by-Step Instructions</h6><ul> <li>Step 1: Find the row for the Parental Type for all three genes.</li> <li>Step 2: Looking at only your two genes, assign PD, NPD, TT.</li> <li>Step 3: Determine if the two genes are linked.</li> <ul><li>PD &gt;&gt; NPD &rarr; linked; PD &approx; NPD &rarr; unlinked</li></ul> <li>Step 4: Determine the map distance between the two genes.</li> <ul><li>D = &half; (TT + 6 NPD) / total = (3 NPD + &half; TT) / total</li></ul></ul><h5>Determine the distance between the two genes MC	<p>70b6_26da</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #5c6419;">Gene J</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #5c6419;"><i>jeweled</i></span>' phenotype. MC	<p>d1d8_a9b4</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #006d61;">Gene E</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #006d61;"><i>elephant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006d61;">Gene E</span> cells absorb excessive amounts of liquid, resulting in giant, swollen cells.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #6041c3;">Gene W</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #6041c3;"><i>webbed</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #6041c3;">Gene W</span> colonies produce delicate, web-like strands that connect neighboring colonies in a cobweb pattern.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: ++, ew, ++, ew"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #1d6e49;">Gene P</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #1d6e49;"><i>pebble</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #1d6e49;">Gene P</span> produces colonies with a rough, uneven surface that resembles a collection of tiny pebbles.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #7c3e9c;">Gene X</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #7c3e9c;"><i>xenon</i></span>' phenotype. Looking at only your two genes, assign PD, NPD, TT.</li> <li>Step 3: Determine if the two genes are linked.</li> <ul><li>PD &gt;&gt; NPD &rarr; linked; PD &approx; NPD &rarr; unlinked</li></ul> <li>Step 4: Determine the map distance between the two genes.</li> <ul><li>D = &half; (TT + 6 NPD) / total = (3 NPD + &half; TT) / total</li></ul></ul><h5>Determine the distance between the two genes MC	<p>f071_9566</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #705c08;">Gene A</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #705c08;"><i>amber</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #705c08;">Gene A</span> cells develop a rich yellow-orange pigmentation, giving the colony a warm, amber hue.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #6041c3;">Gene D</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #6041c3;"><i>doubled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #6041c3;">Gene D</span> cells display double or multiple budding, with several buds emerging simultaneously.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: ++, ad, ++, ad"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #356d1d;">Gene A</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #356d1d;"><i>amber</i></span>' phenotype. MC	<p>dea1_a623</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #1d6e49;">Gene F</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #1d6e49;"><i>fuzzy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #1d6e49;">Gene F</span> colonies are covered in soft, fine filaments, giving them a fuzzy, cotton-like texture.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #7c3e9c;">Gene R</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #7c3e9c;"><i>rusty</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #7c3e9c;">Gene R</span> colonies develop a reddish-brown pigmentation, reminiscent of rusted metal.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: ++, fr, ++, fr"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. Looking at only your two genes, assign PD, NPD, TT.</li> <li>Step 3: Determine if the two genes are linked.</li> <ul><li>PD &gt;&gt; NPD &rarr; linked; PD &approx; NPD &rarr; unlinked</li></ul> <li>Step 4: Determine the map distance between the two genes.</li> <ul><li>D = &half; (TT + 6 NPD) / total = (3 NPD + &half; TT) / total</li></ul></ul><h5>Determine the distance between the two genes MC	<p>b7e6_5853</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #a23025;">Gene A</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #a23025;"><i>amber</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #a23025;">Gene A</span> cells develop a rich yellow-orange pigmentation, giving the colony a warm, amber hue.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #1d6e49;">Gene B</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #1d6e49;"><i>bubbly</i></span>' phenotype. MC	<p>d663_0df6</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #825200;">Gene D</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #825200;"><i>doubled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #825200;">Gene D</span> cells display double or multiple budding, with several buds emerging simultaneously.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006d61;">Gene T</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #006d61;"><i>toxic</i></span>' phenotype. MC	<p>c1fd_45c9</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #825200;">Gene M</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #825200;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #825200;">Gene M</span> colonies are small, dense, and secrete compounds that inhibit the growth of nearby colonies.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #2f6290;">Gene Y</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #2f6290;"><i>yolk</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #2f6290;">Gene Y</span> cells develop a dense, yellowish core that resembles an egg yolk when viewed under a microscope.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: ++, my, ++, my"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>aca6_7cd0</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #705c08;">Gene D</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #705c08;"><i>doubled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #705c08;">Gene D</span> cells display double or multiple budding, with several buds emerging simultaneously.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #7c3e9c;">Gene K</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #7c3e9c;"><i>knotted</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #7c3e9c;">Gene K</span> cells grow in twisted, coiled shapes, resulting in a knotted or gnarled appearance.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: ++, dk, ++, dk"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>626c_6c95</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #91460e;">Gene F</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #91460e;"><i>fuzzy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #91460e;">Gene F</span> colonies are covered in soft, fine filaments, giving them a fuzzy, cotton-like texture.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #2f6290;">Gene H</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #2f6290;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #a23025;">Gene B</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #a23025;"><i>bubbly</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #a23025;">Gene B</span> produces excessive gas bubbles during growth, causing foamy appearance of the media.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #356d1d;">Gene T</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #356d1d;"><i>toxic</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #356d1d;">Gene T</span> secretes a toxic compound that inhibits or kills other microbial colonies nearby.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: ++, bt, ++, bt"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>e184_934a</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #1d6e49;">Gene J</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #1d6e49;"><i>jeweled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #1d6e49;">Gene J</span> colonies appear dotted with tiny, iridescent spots that sparkle under light.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #6041c3;">Gene P</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #6041c3;"><i>pebble</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #6041c3;">Gene P</span> produces colonies with a rough, uneven surface that resembles a collection of tiny pebbles.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: ++, jp, ++, jp"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #1d6e49;">Gene B</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #1d6e49;"><i>bubbly</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #1d6e49;">Gene B</span> produces excessive gas bubbles during growth, causing foamy appearance of the media.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #6041c3;">Gene C</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #6041c3;"><i>clumpy</i></span>' phenotype. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #2f6290;">Gene K</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #2f6290;"><i>knotted</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #2f6290;">Gene K</span> cells grow in twisted, coiled shapes, resulting in a knotted or gnarled appearance.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #973756;">Gene P</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #973756;"><i>pebble</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #973756;">Gene P</span> produces colonies with a rough, uneven surface that resembles a collection of tiny pebbles.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: ++, kp, ++, kp"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>1a0c_f177</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #356d1d;">Gene B</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #356d1d;"><i>bubbly</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #356d1d;">Gene B</span> produces excessive gas bubbles during growth, causing foamy appearance of the media.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #2f6290;">Gene T</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #2f6290;"><i>toxic</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #2f6290;">Gene T</span> secretes a toxic compound that inhibits or kills other microbial colonies nearby.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: ++, bt, ++, bt"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #91460e;">Gene B</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #91460e;"><i>bubbly</i></span>' phenotype. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. MC	<p>cd2a_5237</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #356d1d;">Gene K</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #356d1d;"><i>knotted</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #356d1d;">Gene K</span> cells grow in twisted, coiled shapes, resulting in a knotted or gnarled appearance.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #2f6290;">Gene Y</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #2f6290;"><i>yolk</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #2f6290;">Gene Y</span> cells develop a dense, yellowish core that resembles an egg yolk when viewed under a microscope.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: ++, ky, ++, ky"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #a23025;">Gene D</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #a23025;"><i>doubled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #a23025;">Gene D</span> cells display double or multiple budding, with several buds emerging simultaneously.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #2f6290;">Gene Y</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #2f6290;"><i>yolk</i></span>' phenotype. MC	<p>a85f_be9b</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #2f6290;">Gene D</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #2f6290;"><i>doubled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #2f6290;">Gene D</span> cells display double or multiple budding, with several buds emerging simultaneously.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #973756;">Gene E</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #973756;"><i>elephant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #973756;">Gene E</span> cells absorb excessive amounts of liquid, resulting in giant, swollen cells.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: ++, de, ++, de"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #356d1d;">Gene B</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #356d1d;"><i>bubbly</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #356d1d;">Gene B</span> produces excessive gas bubbles during growth, causing foamy appearance of the media.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #6041c3;">Gene H</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #6041c3;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. MC	<p>189a_5ce4</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #1d6e49;">Gene F</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #1d6e49;"><i>fuzzy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #1d6e49;">Gene F</span> colonies are covered in soft, fine filaments, giving them a fuzzy, cotton-like texture.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #6041c3;">Gene X</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #6041c3;"><i>xenon</i></span>' phenotype. MC	<p>c55c_cb46</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #91460e;">Gene H</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #91460e;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #91460e;">Gene H</span> cells develop long, thread-like filaments that extend outward, creating a hairy, shaggy texture on the colony.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006d61;">Gene K</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #006d61;"><i>knotted</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006d61;">Gene K</span> cells grow in twisted, coiled shapes, resulting in a knotted or gnarled appearance.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: ++, hk, ++, hk"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #a23025;">Gene D</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #a23025;"><i>doubled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #a23025;">Gene D</span> cells display double or multiple budding, with several buds emerging simultaneously.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #3957b2;">Gene M</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #3957b2;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. MC	<p>c681_b056</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #356d1d;">Gene P</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #356d1d;"><i>pebble</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #356d1d;">Gene P</span> produces colonies with a rough, uneven surface that resembles a collection of tiny pebbles.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #6041c3;">Gene W</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #6041c3;"><i>webbed</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #6041c3;">Gene W</span> colonies produce delicate, web-like strands that connect neighboring colonies in a cobweb pattern.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: ++, pw, ++, pw"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #2f6290;">Gene B</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #2f6290;"><i>bubbly</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #2f6290;">Gene B</span> produces excessive gas bubbles during growth, causing foamy appearance of the media.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #973756;">Gene E</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #973756;"><i>elephant</i></span>' phenotype. MC	<p>6eef_821f</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #91460e;">Gene W</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #91460e;"><i>webbed</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #91460e;">Gene W</span> colonies produce delicate, web-like strands that connect neighboring colonies in a cobweb pattern.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006d61;">Gene Y</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #006d61;"><i>yolk</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006d61;">Gene Y</span> cells develop a dense, yellowish core that resembles an egg yolk when viewed under a microscope.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: ++, wy, ++, wy"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>0819_b4e1</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #006886;">Gene M</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #006886;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006886;">Gene M</span> colonies are small, dense, and secrete compounds that inhibit the growth of nearby colonies.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #973756;">Gene X</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #973756;"><i>xenon</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #973756;">Gene X</span> cells emit a faint glow under UV light, as if they were fluorescent.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: ++, mx, ++, mx"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral.
